flashcards.term: Describe the objective, procedure, observation, and principle for Activity 7.1 (To observe chalk disintegration into fine particulate grains.).
flashcards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: describe the objective, procedure, observation, and principle for activity 7.1 (to observe chalk disintegration into fine particulate grains.).]
flashcards.definition:
Aim: To observe chalk disintegration into fine particulate grains.
Materials: Chalk stick, Mortar and pestle, Magnifying glass
Steps: Break chalk stick into fragments. Grind fragments using mortar and pestle into fine powder. Examine powder dust under magnifying glass.
Observation: The finest dust particle remains chalk retaining original chemical properties.
Principle: Macro matter is constructed from sub-microscopic constituent particles.

flashcards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: explain thermal expansion in metals using particle theory.]
flashcards.definition: Heating supplies thermal kinetic energy, causing constituent metal particles to vibrate more vigorously around fixed positions. Increased vibration pushes particles slightly further apart, expanding macro dimensions.

flashcards.term: Explain phase transformations from ice to water to steam using kinetic particle theory.
flashcards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: explain phase transformations from ice to water to steam using kinetic particle theory.]
flashcards.definition: In ice (solid), particles vibrate in fixed grid positions bound by strong forces. Heating supplies thermal kinetic energy; at melting point (0 deg C), energy overcomes rigid attraction to form liquid water with mobile particles. Continued heating raises kinetic energy until boiling point (100 deg C), where particles break free completely into steam gas.
